text:
Arya: Heads up — we need a new synthetic loadgen design to exercise kernel selection, batching heuristics, and KV cache behavior. Current tests are too steady-state and miss p99+/long-tail and burst patterns.

Mike: +1. Real traffic is spiky and heavy-tailed. We should support: QPS ramps, sudden bursts, open-loop vs closed-loop modes, and session affinity to hit KV cache hotness.

Sanjay: For arrival processes, I'd use a mix: baseline Poisson for steady, Pareto for heavy-tail bursts, and scheduled spike events. Also simulate correlated requests from same session to exercise KV reuse.

Kelly: We also need sequence-length and prompt-distribution shaping. In prod we see a bimodal length distribution (short chat turns + long doc completions). That changes batching and kernel selection.

Arya: Agreed. Proposal sketch for generator config (human-readable):

```
mode: mixed
baseline: { qps: 200, arrival: poisson }
bursts:
  - start: 60s, duration: 30s, peak_qps: 2000, shape: pareto(alpha=1.5)
sessions:
  affinity_pct: 40
  reuse_kv: true
length_distribution:
  - short: { pct: 70, tokens: 8 }
  - long:  { pct: 30, tokens: 512 }
retries: { pct: 2, backoff: exp }
closed_loop: { max_concurrency: 500 }
seed: 42
```

Mike: Nice. A few notes:
- Use Poisson for baseline but allow transient overdispersion (NB/compound Poisson) to mimic burstiness.
- For bursts, shape arrival times so we get instantaneous QPS spikes (to test queueing backpressure) and sustained high-phase to test overload fallbacks.
- Provide both QPS-driven (open-loop) and concurrency-driven (closed-loop) modes to exercise batching scheduling differences.

Sanjay: On KV cache behavior: we must simulate cold-starts for some sessions and hot keys for others. Add a hot-key ratio and TTL semantics so cache eviction interacts with request pattern. Example: 10% of sessions generate 70% of tokens for a hot prefix.

Kelly: Also capture model routing fallbacks: some test runs should toggle kernel variants mid-run to validate graceful handoff and performance deltas. E.g., switch to quantized kernel at t=120s.

PerfBot: Automated profiling runs from last week show a 12% p99 regression when sequence lengths shift from 16->256 under current batching heuristics. Logs: 
```
perf_summary:
  run: 2024-11-09T14:12:00Z
  baseline_p99: 210ms
  test_p99: 235ms
  dominant_source: batching_mismatch + kernel_sel_suboptimal
```

Arya: That's exactly why we need apples-to-apples comparisons. Test harness must pin: model version, hardware, kernel flags, batcher config, and request trace seed. Otherwise baseline vs experiment is noisy.

Mike: For apples-to-apples, include deterministic replay mode that consumes a recorded trace (anonymized) and replays timing/sequence lengths exactly. Also include a paramized synthetic mode to sweep distributions (e.g., Pareto alpha, burst amplitude).

Sanjay: Replay harness design notes: capture trace fields -> { relative_ts, user_id_hash, prompt_length, tokens_generated, route_hint }. Strip PII, keep seedable rng for prompt sampling. Support rate-scaling factor so we can sweep higher QPS than observed.

Kelly: Need metrics emitted per-request for comparison: model_variant, kernel_selected, batch_size, queue_time_ms, server_compute_ms, kv_hit(bool), kv_latency_ms, trace_id. Make these ingestible by existing perf dashboards.

Arya: Also think about long-run degradation tests (hours) to surface memory/amortized kernel warmups and KV eviction patterns. Short spikes won't show leak-y behavior.

LoadGenBot: Tip: include a "tail_shaper" option that injects rare long requests following a Pareto-Lévy distribution to reproduce p999+ tails. Example param: tail_alpha=1.2, tail_frequency=0.5% of requests.

Mike: Implementation checklist: 
- [ ] New generator binary with mixed-mode arrivals
- [ ] Config schema + example presets (chat, doc, low-latency, heavy-throughput)
- [ ] Replay harness that can anonymize + seed traces
- [ ] Metrics enrichment for kernel & KV signals
- [ ] Canary runs comparing old vs new batcher/kernels under identical trace/seed

Sanjay: We should also automate regression scoring: p50/p95/p99/p999 latency, cpu/gpu utilization, token/sec, cost-estimates (tokens * kernel_cost). Fail if p99 regresses > 5% or p999 > 3%.

Kelly: Small UX point — make it easy to express "burst schedule" as human tuples: e.g., `[(t=60s, 5s burst, +3x), (t=300s, 30s burst, +10x)]`. That helps non-devs run scenarios.

Arya: OK next steps: I'll spec a JSON config + proto for trace anonymization and iterate on generator CLI. Mike/Sanjay/Kelly — can you review the config presets? I'll aim to land a PoC in the perf repo by EOD Friday.

Mike: I'll take the replay harness stub.

Sanjay: I'll draft KV hotkey workload generator and TTL model.

Kelly: I'll wire metrics into dashboards and add regression gates.

PerfBot: Scheduled test job queued: `perf/runs/loadgen-longtail/1743001234` :rocket:

Arya: Thanks all — please drop short comments in this thread with config ideas or sample traces.

Kelly: Quick question — do we want to simulate client-side retries + exponential backoff? That changes queueing dynamic.

Mike: Yes, include a retry policy toggle. Set default to off for clean comparisons, and enable in a separate scenario.

Arya: Noted. I'll add `retries: none | prod-like | aggressive` presets.

LoadGenBot: Saved preset examples: `chat_lowlatency`, `doc_highthroughput`, `mixed_longtail`. Use `--preset mixed_longtail --scale 2.0` to run.

Sanjay: One last thought — instrument kernel selection decision path (why a kernel was chosen) and attach to traces. Helps debug regressions in selection heuristics.

Arya: Great call. Add `kernel_decision_log: true` as a togglable flag.

Mike: Perfect. I posted a minimal config PR to the perf repo for review: https://git.internal/redwood/perf/pull/312

Arya: Reviewing now. Thanks everyone.
